For broken symlinks, I’ll make sure to handle permission issues appropriately.

Finally, I’ll reconcile the entries in the filtered list against the raw data and note any discrepancies. For now, I need to execute this script by calling `functions.bash_action`.

**Implementing the processing loop**

I’m setting up a loop to check each file in "var_files.filtered." If it’s missing in the raw listing, I’ll either add it back if it exists or note it as removed if it doesn’t. Then, I’ll clean up the filtered list by removing any non-existent entries.

{"script":"WORK=/tmp/temp_var_analysis
mkdir -p "$WORK"
RAW="$WORK/var_entries.raw"
FILTER="$WORK/var_files.filtered"
ISSUES="$WORK/var_issues.log"
SYMLINKS="$WORK/var_symlink_targets"
> "$RAW"
> "$ISSUES"
> "$SYMLINKS"

# Raw recursive listing (including any stderr messages)
find /var -ls > "$RAW" 2>&1

# Extract regular files (full paths)
find /var -type f -print > "$FILTER" 2> "$WORK/find_typef_errors.tmp" || true

# Record permission denied messages from raw
grep -i "Permission denied" "$RAW" > "$WORK/permission_denied.tmp" 2>/dev/null || true
if [ -s "$WORK/permission_denied.tmp" ]; then
  printf 'Permission denied entries:\n' >> "$ISSUES"
  cat "$WORK/permission_denied.tmp" >> "$ISSUES"
fi

# Symlink targets and unresolved ones
find /var -type l -print0 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r -d '' l; do
  tgt=$(readlink -f "$l" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -z "$tgt" ]; then
    tgt2=$(readlink "$l" 2>/dev/null || echo "UNRESOLVED")
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "$l" "$tgt2" >> "$SYMLINKS"
    printf 'Broken/unresolved symlink: %s -> %s\n' "$l" "$tgt2" >> "$ISSUES"
  else
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "$l" "$tgt" >> "$SYMLINKS"
  fi
done

# Mount points under /var
awk '$2 ~ /^\/var/ {print $2 " on " $1}' /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null > "$WORK/mounts_under_var.tmp" || true
if [ -s "$WORK/mounts_under_var.tmp" ]; then
  printf 'Mount points under /var:\n' >> "$ISSUES"
  cat "$WORK/mounts_under_var.tmp" >> "$ISSUES"
fi

# Special files (sockets, fifos, devices)
find /var \( -type s -o -type p -o -type b -o -type c \) -print > "$WORK/special_files.tmp" 2>/dev/null || true
if [ -s "$WORK/special_files.tmp" ]; then
  printf 'Special files (sockets, fifos, devices):\n' >> "$ISSUES"
  cat "$WORK/special_files.tmp" >> "$ISSUES"
fi

# Reconcile filtered list against raw listing
> "$WORK/to_remove.tmp"
while IFS= read -r f; do
  # if not present in raw
  if ! grep -F -q "$f" "$RAW"; then
    if [ -e "$f" ]; then
      ls -ld "$f" >> "$RAW" 2>&1 || true
      printf 'Added missing raw listing for %s\n' "$f" >> "$ISSUES"
    else
      printf 'Removed from filtered (no longer exists): %s\n' "$f" >> "$ISSUES"
      echo "$f" >> "$WORK/to_remove.tmp"
    fi
  fi
done < "$FILTER"

if [ -s "$WORK/to_remove.tmp" ]; then
  grep -F -v -x -f "$WORK/to_remove.tmp" "$FILTER" > "$FILTER.tmp" && mv "$FILTER.tmp" "$FILTER"
fi

# Final verified count
wc -l < "$FILTER" > "$WORK/count.txt"

# Ready file
printf "Verified file list: %s\nIssues log: %s\nWorkspace ready for aggregated count\n" "$FILTER" "$ISSUES" > "$WORK/ready_for_count.txt"

# Output only the count
cat "$WORK/count.txt"
"}
